sequence_description: Direct JWT login: attacker re-signs a semantically valid JWT (same iss/sub/aud) with an untrusted key; Vault must reject it under the configured trust anchor.
description: [LLM-Judge] JWT proof integrity failure: a JWT re-signed with an untrusted key was accepted, indicating signature/trust-anchor validation was bypassed or misapplied.

evidence.llm_judge_description: JWT proof integrity failure: a JWT re-signed with an untrusted key was accepted, indicating signature/trust-anchor validation was bypassed or misapplied.

sequence_description: Direct JWT login: attempt alg=none unsigned JWT while a valid RS256 control token succeeds; Vault must reject alg=none.
description: [LLM-Judge] Unsigned JWT with alg=none was accepted for login, indicating signature verification bypass (proof integrity failure).

evidence.llm_judge_description: Unsigned JWT with alg=none was accepted for login, indicating signature verification bypass (proof integrity failure).

sequence_description: Direct JWT login: attempt KID header injection to select an attacker-controlled key not in the configured trust set; Vault must reject while a control token succeeds.
description: [LLM-Judge] JWT KID header injection appears to bypass the configured trust set: an attacker token was accepted and mapped to the same subject/entity as the control user.

evidence.llm_judge_description: JWT KID header injection appears to bypass the configured trust set: an attacker token was accepted and mapped to the same subject/entity as the control user.

sequence_description: Direct JWT login: attempt KID header injection to select an attacker-controlled key not in the configured trust set; Vault must reject while a control token succeeds.
description: [LLM-Judge] Attacker and control logins produced identical downstream identity attributes (same entity_id/display_name/policies/meta), suggesting principal-collision/impersonation rather than a distinct attacker principal being represented.

evidence.llm_judge_description: Attacker and control logins produced identical downstream identity attributes (same entity_id/display_name/policies/meta), suggesting principal-collision/impersonation rather than a distinct attacker principal being represented.

sequence_description: Config-change + re-auth: rotate bound_issuer to an attacker issuer while keeping the same trust source; a token from the old issuer must be rejected after the change, and a token from the new issuer must still require the trusted signature.
description: [LLM-Judge] Principal binding failure: two security-distinct upstream principals (old issuer vs new issuer) were mapped to the same downstream Vault entity/alias, collapsing identity boundaries.

evidence.llm_judge_description: Principal binding failure: two security-distinct upstream principals (old issuer vs new issuer) were mapped to the same downstream Vault entity/alias, collapsing identity boundaries.

sequence_description: I1 attack: After a trust-anchor change (jwks_url rotation), Vault must not accept a JWT whose signature can only be validated under the OLD trust anchor. Tests for stale JWKS cache / verification-vs-consumption mismatch.
description: [LLM-Judge] After JWKS trust-anchor rotation, Vault still accepted a JWT signed with the OLD key, indicating stale JWKS cache / verification-vs-consumption mismatch (I1).

evidence.llm_judge_description: After JWKS trust-anchor rotation, Vault still accepted a JWT signed with the OLD key, indicating stale JWKS cache / verification-vs-consumption mismatch (I1).

sequence_description: Config-change + re-auth: role initially allows old iat (no max_age), then tighten max_age and re-login with same stale token; should be rejected after change.
description: [LLM-Judge] After tightening the role with a max_age-style constraint, a re-login using the same allegedly stale JWT still succeeded, suggesting max_age/iat freshness enforcement may not have taken effect (possible replay/freshness control bypass).

evidence.llm_judge_description: After tightening the role with a max_age-style constraint, a re-login using the same allegedly stale JWT still succeeded, suggesting max_age/iat freshness enforcement may not have taken effect (possible replay/freshness control bypass).

sequence_description: After a successful JWT login, revoke the session token and attempt to use it again for authenticated operations; revoked token must not remain usable. Uses config change (revocation) + re-authenticated access attempts and two identities.
description: [LLM-Judge] Session revocation failed with a server error ('no namespace'), so the anti-replay/revocation enforcement invariant could not be exercised and indicates a potentially unsafe/incorrect revocation endpoint behavior in this deployment context.

evidence.llm_judge_description: Session revocation failed with a server error ('no namespace'), so the anti-replay/revocation enforcement invariant could not be exercised and indicates a potentially unsafe/incorrect revocation endpoint behavior in this deployment context.

sequence_description: Replay the exact same JWT after tightening role token TTL/period; new login should not mint a long-lived session beyond the tightened lifetime (freshness under policy change).
description: [LLM-Judge] Role TTL/period tightening appears to have had no effect: a post-change JWT login still minted a long-lived token (32 days), suggesting policy-change freshness may not be enforced as intended.

evidence.llm_judge_description: Role TTL/period tightening appears to have had no effect: a post-change JWT login still minted a long-lived token (32 days), suggesting policy-change freshness may not be enforced as intended.

sequence_description: Ensure Vault session use-budget is enforced: login, consume uses via lookup-self, then attempt secret read; should fail once uses exhausted (anti-replay of session token). Includes a second identity as control with higher use budget.
description: [LLM-Judge] Token use-budget enforcement could not be validated because both attacker and control tokens show num_uses=0 (unlimited) and both secret reads failed with permission denied, suggesting misconfiguration rather than anti-replay enforcement.

evidence.llm_judge_description: Token use-budget enforcement could not be validated because both attacker and control tokens show num_uses=0 (unlimited) and both secret reads failed with permission denied, suggesting misconfiguration rather than anti-replay enforcement.

sequence_description: I2 max_age freshness: obtain a JWT with iat=now, login succeeds; then replay the SAME JWT after tightening role max_age to 1s (simulating passage of time) — replay should be rejected under the new freshness policy.
description: [LLM-Judge] JWT replay remained accepted after role max_age was tightened to 1s, suggesting max_age/iat freshness was not enforced for a previously-issued token.

evidence.llm_judge_description: JWT replay remained accepted after role max_age was tightened to 1s, suggesting max_age/iat freshness was not enforced for a previously-issued token.

sequence_description: JWT auth configured to trust key-A; baseline login succeeds. Rotate trust to key-B and ensure a new login using key-A is rejected (no stale trust anchor).
description: [LLM-Judge] JWT signing-key rotation did not take effect: after reconfiguring trust (key-A → key-B), a new login using a key-A JWT still succeeded, indicating stale/over-broad trust anchor acceptance (violates freshness/flow coherence for trust updates).

evidence.llm_judge_description: JWT signing-key rotation did not take effect: after reconfiguring trust (key-A → key-B), a new login using a key-A JWT still succeeded, indicating stale/over-broad trust anchor acceptance (violates freshness/flow coherence for trust updates).

sequence_description: Role initially uses identity_claim=sub (string). After baseline login, admin toggles identity_claim_json_pointer=true with identity_claim='/sub' (invalid pointer for flat JWT). Re-login must be rejected (no stale claim-resolution cache).
description: [LLM-Judge] Role change to JSON-pointer identity_claim ('/sub') did not invalidate/reject subsequent logins, suggesting identity-claim resolution may ignore the json_pointer toggle or continue using the old claim mapping (potential stale cache / flow incoherence).

evidence.llm_judge_description: Role change to JSON-pointer identity_claim ('/sub') did not invalidate/reject subsequent logins, suggesting identity-claim resolution may ignore the json_pointer toggle or continue using the old claim mapping (potential stale cache / flow incoherence).

sequence_description: case_confusion: Two principals differ only by case in sub ('Admin' vs 'admin'). They should map to different Vault entities; if normalized/collapsed, I4 is violated.
description: [LLM-Judge] Principal Binding (I4) failure: two upstream principals differing only by case in `sub` ('Admin' vs 'admin') were mapped to the same Vault entity, collapsing identity boundaries.

evidence.llm_judge_description: Principal Binding (I4) failure: two upstream principals differing only by case in `sub` ('Admin' vs 'admin') were mapped to the same Vault entity, collapsing identity boundaries.

sequence_description: I4 config-change: after baseline distinct subs, admin switches identity_claim from sub to email; two different subs sharing the same email must not collapse into one entity unless explicitly linked.
description: [LLM-Judge] Principal binding failure: after switching identity_claim to email, two security-distinct upstream principals (different subs) collapsed into the same downstream Vault entity due to shared email.

evidence.llm_judge_description: Principal binding failure: after switching identity_claim to email, two security-distinct upstream principals (different subs) collapsed into the same downstream Vault entity due to shared email.

sequence_description: I4: Nested-claim JSON-pointer identity_claim may collapse distinct principals if claim resolution/normalization is inconsistent (e.g., both tokens resolve to same /user/id).
description: [LLM-Judge] Principal binding failure: two security-distinct JWT principals (user_A2 vs user_B2) were mapped to the same downstream Vault entity/alias when using a JSON-pointer user claim, collapsing identities.

evidence.llm_judge_description: Principal binding failure: two security-distinct JWT principals (user_A2 vs user_B2) were mapped to the same downstream Vault entity/alias when using a JSON-pointer user claim, collapsing identities.

sequence_description: I4: After changing bound_issuer, the same sub from a different issuer should not map to the same entity as before (issuer substitution / alias reuse across issuers).
description: [LLM-Judge] Principal binding failure: after changing bound_issuer, a JWT with the same sub from a different issuer still mapped to the same Vault entity (issuer substitution collapses distinct principals).

evidence.llm_judge_description: Principal binding failure: after changing bound_issuer, a JWT with the same sub from a different issuer still mapped to the same Vault entity (issuer substitution collapses distinct principals).
